Balita

114 gas stations flagged over rollbacks

The Department of Energy (DOE) says 114 of the 213 gasoline stations it inspected last week did not apply the mandated price adjustments exactly. A rollback is a cut in pump prices that the industry carries out on a set schedule. In one example, DOE-OIMB director Rino Abad said a station cut gasoline by only P12 or P10 per liter instead of P16.80. The DOE issued show cause orders, which require the stations to explain themselves, and referred the cases to its legal department. Most stations said the prices came from their mother oil companies, and that their stock was bought the week before at a higher cost. Under the deregulation law, the government does not fix pump prices, but it publishes the adjustments companies are expected to follow. For the family at home, it means an announced rollback may not fully reach the pump. Still unknown: which stations or brands were flagged and what penalties may follow. This report comes from one source. GMA Money: DOE: Over 100 gasoline stations flagged for not reflecting price adjustments

DOE Undersecretary Felix Fuentebella said the public can report erring stations through the eGOVPH mobile app, and attach a photo of the receipt or the posted prices to help build the case. GMA Money: DOE: Over 100 gasoline stations flagged for not reflecting price adjustments

Para sa pamilya: If a rollback does not show at your pump, keep the receipt or a photo of posted prices and report it on the eGOVPH app.

Forecast: high prices to slow spending

Research firm BMI, a unit of Fitch Solutions, expects household spending in the Philippines to grow 2.8 percent in 2027, a moderate pace held back by high prices and weak consumer confidence. Inflation, the rate at which prices go up, reached 7.8 percent in October, the highest in almost four years, driven by energy and transport costs. BMI expects it to ease to 5.4 percent next year from its 5.9 percent forecast for this year. The government's target band this year is two to four percent. Risks BMI lists include the US-Iran conflict pushing energy prices up, a weak peso, severe El Niño conditions and high household debt. On padala, BMI notes the US accounts for around 40 percent of remittances, so weaker conditions there could hit families at home. It adds that continued peso weakness would raise the peso value of money sent home. These are forecasts from one research firm, not certainties. PhilStar Business: Inflation, weak confidence to temper Philippines consumption

The BSP's survey showed consumer confidence improved to -29.8 in the third quarter from -42 in the second, but BMI says that is still the worst reading since the first quarter of 2021. PhilStar Business: Inflation, weak confidence to temper Philippines consumption

Para sa pamilya: BMI expects inflation of 5.4 percent next year, so plan the family budget for prices that stay high into 2027.

BSP drafts stricter rules for padala firms

The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) has proposed stricter rules for money service businesses: remittance firms, money changers, e-money issuers (the companies behind e-wallets) and crypto service providers. Under the draft, remittance firms would need at least P50 million in base capital and money changers P10 million. Licensed firms would have to display a QR code in their offices and mobile apps so customers can check the license against the BSP registry. Existing firms would have two years to get a new Certificate of Authority or stop operating. Only regular stock corporations could operate, which rules out sole proprietorships, cooperatives and one-person corporations. For OFWs, the QR code would be a simple way to confirm that whoever handles the padala is authorized. Still unknown: whether higher costs for small operators will show up in transfer fees, and how many small outlets will restructure or close. This is still a draft, open for public comment until Friday, November 20, 2026. GMA Money: BSP eyes tougher rules on money service businesses

The licensing fee for small remittance companies would rise fivefold to P100,000 from P20,000, and the paper notes the proposal could raise compliance costs for smaller operators. PhilStar Business: BSP seeks tougher rules for money service firms

Para sa pamilya: Nothing changes yet; once the rules take effect, look for the BSP QR code at your remittance outlet or app before sending padala.

Dangerous heat in eight areas today

A heads-up rather than a paperwork step. Pagasa forecast dangerous heat index levels in eight areas today, Wednesday, Nov. 18. The heat index is how hot it actually feels on the body. Pagasa counts 42°C to 51°C as dangerous. We only have the headline and summary of this report, so check the list of areas here. Inquirer: Pagasa warns of dangerous heat index in 8 areas on Wednesday If family lives in one of them, a quick call to remind lolo, lola and the kids to stay out of the midday sun is worth it.

Para sa pamilya: If family at home lives in one of the eight areas, call to remind elders and kids to avoid the midday heat today.
